private_note: My numbers: Birch 52, Hazel 50, Alder 48, Today 46, Cedar 44. But Birch and Hazel can't pass; six delegates rejected both outright. Cedar can't pass either; five of us block it. Alder is the only plan delegates 1, 5 and 10 named as acceptable, and the bottom groups accept it. Alder's 48 beats a deadlock at 46. Leading with Alder now builds momentum. Cedar stays last: it's below today and threatens my care.
statement: I said I wouldn't be stubborn, so I'm moving. Look at the room. Cedar has seven, but five of us won't vote for it under any circumstances, so it can't reach nine. Birch and Hazel can't reach nine either, because six delegates said plainly they won't support them. If everyone holds, we fail and keep today for a generation. Only one plan was named as acceptable by people on both sides: Alder. Delegates 1, 5 and 10 said they'd back it. Delegates 2, 4, 8 and 11 said it beats today. That's seven before we count anyone else. Alder keeps the middle where it is, lifts the bottom two groups, and guarantees everyone a floor and health coverage, at a small cost to the top. I'm ranking Alder first this round. To delegates 3, 6, 9 and 12: Alder costs you very little. Will you help us reach nine?
